name: Federal W-4 Form (2024)
description: Employee's Withholding Certificate - IRS Form W-4 (Rev. December 2020)

fields.label: Personal Information
fields.help_text: Enter your personal information as it appears on your Social Security card

fields.label: First Name
fields.help_text: Enter your legal first name

fields.label: Last Name
fields.help_text: Enter your legal last name

fields.label: Social Security Number
fields.help_text: Enter your 9-digit Social Security Number (XXX-XX-XXXX)

fields.label: Home Address
fields.help_text: Enter your current home address

fields.label: Step 1: Enter Personal Information
fields.help_text: Complete Steps 1-4 ONLY if they apply to you; otherwise, skip to Step 5

fields.label: Filing Status

options.label: Single or Married filing separately
options.description: Check this box if you file as Single or if you are Married filing separately

options.label: Married filing jointly or Qualifying surviving spouse
options.description: Check this box if you are Married filing jointly or are a Qualifying surviving spouse

options.label: Head of household
options.description: Check this box ONLY if you file as Head of household (generally, you're unmarried and pay more than half the costs of keeping up a home for yourself and a qualifying individual)

fields.help_text: Select your tax filing status

fields.label: Step 2: Multiple Jobs or Spouse Works
fields.help_text: Complete this step if you (1) hold more than one job at a time, or (2) are married filing jointly and your spouse also works. The correct amount of withholding depends on income earned from all of these jobs.

fields.label: Choose ONE of the following options:

options.label: Not applicable - I have only one job and my spouse doesn't work
options.description: Skip Step 2 if you only have one job and no working spouse

options.label: Use the IRS Tax Withholding Estimator
options.description: RECOMMENDED. Use the online estimator at www.irs.gov/W4App for most accurate withholding. Enter the result in Step 4(c).

options.label: Use the Multiple Jobs Worksheet
options.description: Complete the Multiple Jobs Worksheet on page 3 and enter the result in Step 4(c). If you choose this option, you must also check the box in Step 2(c).

options.label: Check the box in Step 2(c) (if only 2 jobs total)
options.description: If there are only two jobs total, you may check this box. Do the same on Form W-4 for the other job. This option is accurate for jobs with similar pay; otherwise, more tax than necessary may be withheld.

fields.help_text: Choose the method that best fits your situation

fields.label: Step 2(c): Two Jobs, Similar Pay
fields.help_text: Check this box ONLY if you have exactly 2 jobs with similar pay, and you've checked the same box on the other job's W-4

fields.label: Step 3: Claim Dependents
fields.help_text: If your total income will be $200,000 or less ($400,000 or less if married filing jointly), complete this step

fields.label: Are you eligible to claim dependents?

options.label: No - My income exceeds the threshold or I have no dependents
options.description: Skip to Step 4 if your income exceeds $200,000 (single) or $400,000 (married filing jointly)

options.label: Yes - I am eligible to claim dependents
options.description: Complete the fields below to calculate your dependent credits

fields.label: Number of qualifying children under age 17
fields.help_text: Multiply by $2,000. Enter the result in the calculation below.

fields.label: Number of other dependents
fields.help_text: Multiply by $500. Enter the result in the calculation below.

fields.label: Step 3 Total Credit Amount
fields.help_text: This will be automatically calculated based on the number of dependents entered above

fields.label: Step 4: Other Adjustments (optional)
fields.help_text: Complete this step if you want tax withheld for other income, or if you want to reduce withholding for deductions or extra withholding per pay period

fields.label: Step 4(a): Other income (not from jobs)
fields.help_text: If you want tax withheld for other income you expect this year that won't have withholding, enter the amount of other income here (e.g., interest, dividends, retirement income). This may include income from self-employment, interest, dividends, etc.

fields.label: Step 4(b): Deductions
fields.help_text: If you expect to claim deductions other than the standard deduction and want to reduce your withholding, use the Deductions Worksheet on page 3 and enter the result here

fields.label: Step 4(c): Extra withholding per pay period
fields.help_text: Enter any additional tax you want withheld each pay period. This can help you avoid owing taxes when you file your return.

fields.label: Step 5: Sign Here
fields.help_text: Under penalties of perjury, I declare that this certificate, to the best of my knowledge and belief, is true, correct, and complete.

fields.label: Employee Signature
fields.help_text: Sign your name using the signature pad below

fields.label: Date Signed
fields.help_text: Date you signed this form

fields.label: Employer Information (to be completed by employer)
fields.help_text: This section will be automatically filled by your employer

fields.label: Employer Name
fields.help_text: This will be filled automatically by your employer

fields.label: Employer Address
fields.help_text: This will be filled automatically by your employer

fields.label: Employer EIN
fields.help_text: Employer Identification Number (will be filled by employer)

fields.label: First Date of Employment
fields.help_text: This will be filled automatically by your employer

validation_rules.message: You must enter the number of qualifying children and other dependents when claiming dependents
You can only check Step 2(c) if you selected that option in Step 2

instructions.general: Complete Form W-4 so that your employer can withhold the correct federal income tax from your pay. Give Form W-4 to your employer. Your withholding is subject to review by the IRS.
when_to_use: When you start a new job
When you want to adjust your withholding
When your personal or financial situation changes
instructions.exempt_status: If you claim exemption, you will have no income tax withheld from your paycheck and may owe taxes and penalties when you file your tax return. To claim exemption from withholding, certify that you meet both of the conditions by writing 'Exempt' on Form W-4 in the space below Step 4(c).
instructions.privacy_act_notice: We ask for the information on this form to carry out the Internal Revenue laws of the United States. Internal Revenue Code sections 3402(f)(2) and 6109 require you to provide this information; your employer uses it to determine your federal income tax withholding. Failure to provide a properly completed form will result in your being treated as a single person with no other entries on the form.
